diagnostic_evidence.quote: Throughout this work, we use the classical Sobolev spaces.
The mapping $F:\widehat{D}_h\rightarrow D$ is piecewise $C^{k+1}$ continuous
The global interploation $F_h\in \mathbb{C}(\widehat{D}_h)$ is defined by

issues.failure_explanation: The construction provides a continuous, piecewise-smooth auxiliary map, not a globally C1 map. Its Jacobian and determinant can jump across the images of reference-element interfaces, so they generally do not belong to classical W^{1,infinity}(D). The first-order estimate in eq2.2 does not establish global second derivatives; H3 supplies only elementwise derivative bounds.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the global W^{1,infinity}(D) norms by elementwise norms over F(widehat K), and derive these bounds using H3 and interpolation stability.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted global Sobolev regularity is unjustified. Geometric derivative estimates must instead be formulated locally, without inferring cross-interface Lipschitz continuity.
issues.title: Global Jacobian regularity is asserted for a piecewise-smooth map
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of the regularity statement; the uniform elementwise bounds needed by the method can be retained without changing its convergence rate.

issues.failure_explanation: An L2 projection onto degree-k polynomials does not have an O(h^{k+1}) error in H^{k+1}. Indeed, the derivatives of order k+1 of the projection vanish, so those derivatives of the error equal those of the original function. The displayed transition therefore cannot establish the claimed boundary approximation rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the scaled trace inequality with h^{-1} times the squared L2 error and h times the squared H1 error, together with the standard projection estimates of orders h^{k+1} and h^k respectively.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary contribution in the proof of the DG approximation estimate is not established by eq3.3.
issues.title: The projection error is assigned an unavailable high-Sobolev-norm rate
issues.why_classification: The correct trace argument is a routine local replacement and preserves the lemma's statement and the final convergence rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: From the definition of the DG norm, applying Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the boundedness of $\sigma$, it is straightforward to observe that

issues.failure_explanation: The L4 term requires control of the individual interior trace of the projection error, whereas its DG norm controls only interior jumps, boundary traces, and volume values. On an interior affine patch with sigma=1, smooth functions with zero local polynomial moments can concentrate in a thin layer around a face while retaining a nonzero common trace. Their projection errors have DG norm tending to zero, but L4 against a fixed discontinuous test function remains nonzero. Thus the asserted DG-norm continuity is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq3.4 by a bound of order h^{k+1/2} times the H^{k+1} norm of the extended solution and the DG norm of the test function, using separate one-sided projection trace estimates. Modify eq3.19 accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The continuity lemma and its use in the error decomposition eq3.19 are unsupported.
issues.title: The DG norm does not control the one-sided interior trace in the flux term
issues.why_classification: The stated continuity claim must be weakened and its flux argument replaced, but a contained approximation argument can preserve the main error rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that there exist two positive constants $m$ and $M$ such that $0<m\leq\sigma\leq M$.
Suppose that the assumptions $(H_1\sim H_3)$ and $(A_1\sim A_2)$ hold.

issues.failure_explanation: The positive lower bound on sigma is imposed only in the stability lemma, not in Lemma 3.2 or the main theorem. Their arguments nevertheless require L2 norms to be controlled by the DG norm. For the allowed case sigma=0, a nonzero element bubble with zero traces has zero DG quantity but positive L2 norm. Thus the needed coercive norm comparison is unavailable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the existing condition 0<m<=sigma<=M a standing hypothesis for the DG error analysis, including Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 3.1, on the computational domain.
issues.overall_effect: The DG-norm continuity and consistency estimates are not justified for the full stated bounded-absorption class.
issues.title: The error estimates omit the positive-absorption hypothesis needed for coercivity
issues.why_classification: This narrows the coefficient class rather than merely correcting notation, but retains the method and rate in the positive-absorption regime already used for stability.

issues.failure_explanation: A small displacement controls a function difference through its gradient, not through its L2 norm alone. Rapidly varying smooth functions invalidate eq3.9. Moreover, the H1 term explicitly present in eq3.10 contributes h^{2k+1} times the squared H1 norm after applying the trace estimate; eq3.11 silently replaces it by an L2 norm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a valid composition-difference estimate and replace the leading L2 norm in Lemma 3.3 by an H1 norm, using norms on a suitable common region. The main theorem's H^{k+1} term can absorb this corrected derivative dependence.
issues.overall_effect: The stated norm dependence in Lemma 3.3 and the ensuing bound for T1 are not established.
issues.title: The pullback difference is bounded without the necessary first derivatives
issues.why_classification: The auxiliary lemma's quantitative claim must be weakened, although a contained translation-and-trace argument preserves the final h-order.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we extend the solution $I$ in (\ref{eq1.1}) to a function $\tilde{I}$ defined on the hold-all region $D_H = \text{convex}(D \cup D_h)$
the auxiliary mapping $\Phi_h = F_h\circ F^{-1}:D\rightarrow D_h$

issues.failure_explanation: The pullback samples the solution throughout D, but the right-hand side measures it only on D_h. For an allowed inward approximation D_h strictly contained in D, take sigma=1 and a smooth nonzero solution supported in D outside the closure of D_h, with source manufactured from the PDE. Its smooth extension has every displayed norm on D_h equal to zero, while I composed with Phi_h^{-1} is nonzero on D_h. This directly contradicts eq3.8, independently of the missing derivative in eq3.9.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State global regularity of the extension on D_H, prove the composition estimates there, and replace the affected solution norms in the lemma and final estimate by norms on D_H or a controlled common neighborhood.
issues.overall_effect: The pullback comparison and the main theorem's use of it cannot be justified solely by the stated computational-domain solution norms.
issues.title: Computational-domain norms cannot control values sampled outside that domain
issues.why_classification: The repair changes the region and regularity control appearing in the estimates, but the paper already introduces a hold-all extension and the same convergence order can be retained.

for positive constants $c_1, c_2$ independent of $h$ and the face $F$.

Under the shape-regularity and quasi-uniformity of $\mathcal{T}_h$, the total length of the discrete zero level set remains bounded independently of $h$

issues.failure_explanation: A2 allows the gradient at a regular zero to tend to zero with h; it supplies neither uniform tubular constants nor uniform level-set measure. For example, near a smooth boundary y=x^4 with horizontal direction, quadratic boundary interpolants can have simple grazing zeros with slope of order h^2, while the band |Omega dot n_h|<=C h^2 has width of order h^{2/3}, not h^2. The proof also omits faces with no zero even though their small-value band can be nonempty.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen A2 to quantitative h-uniform transversality and level-set/chart control on a fixed small-value neighborhood, prove a band estimate that includes zero-free faces, and restrict the dependent results to that narrower geometric class.
issues.overall_effect: The grazing-band and inflow symmetric-difference estimates are unsupported under A1–A2, so the central boundary-consistency argument does not establish the advertised scope.
issues.title: Qualitative regular values do not imply the claimed uniform grazing-band measure
issues.why_classification: The stated hypotheses admit degenerately grazing geometries for which the claimed measure rate is false. Repair requires excluding that admitted regime or replacing the central geometric estimate and its downstream argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Even a valid small-area estimate does not locate every point of the set near a zero level set. On a piecewise-smooth boundary, normal jumps can also skip the value zero, so small normal components need not imply proximity to an actual discrete zero. This inference would remain invalid after merely establishing Lemma 3.5's area bound. The desired small-normal conclusion, however, follows directly from eq3.14 and the opposite-sign condition.

failure_location.quote: Lemma \ref{lemma3.5} implies that any $x \in \Gamma^{-}_h \Delta \Phi_h(\Gamma^{-})$ satisfies $\operatorname{dist}(x, \Gamma^0_h) \lesssim h^k$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the distance inference and derive eq3.17 directly from eq3.14 by considering the signs defining the symmetric difference.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted pointwise localization is unproved, although the normal-component estimate used later can be retained.
issues.title: A measure estimate is incorrectly converted into pointwise distance control
issues.why_classification: An already available pointwise estimate gives a short local bypass with no loss of the lemma's normal-component conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $f_h\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)$ and $I_h$ be the numerical solution of (\ref{eq2.4}).

issues.failure_explanation: Regularity of the pulled-back original source f_h does not establish regularity or a bound for the residual of the chosen solution extension, tilde f, on D_h, especially outside D. Only boundedness of sigma and broken H^{k+1} and W^{1,infinity} regularity of tilde I are supplied; these do not imply that tilde f is W^{1,infinity}. No compatible residual-extension estimate relates the norm introduced in eq3.23 to the f_h norm in the theorem. Consequently the volume consistency estimate cannot be closed with the stated hypotheses and right-hand side.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify compatible coefficient and residual extensions on D_H, require tilde f to be globally W^{1,infinity} there, and state the error bound with its controlled norm rather than the unconnected f_h norm.
issues.overall_effect: The E1 estimate does not prove the source-dependent term in eq3.18.
issues.title: The consistency proof requires an uncontrolled residual extension
issues.why_classification: A stronger extension hypothesis and a changed data norm give a comparable estimate with the same h-order, but the theorem as stated promises more than the proof supports.

issues.failure_explanation: Whole quasi-uniform elements touching a codimension-two grazing set form a patch with volume generally of order h^2, independently of k. In two dimensions, even one such element already has area comparable to h^2, contradicting the asserted O(h^{k+1}) bound for k>=2. A surface strip of measure O(h^k) does not give that volume for its covering mesh cells. Inclusion of all mismatch points in the particular patch D_c is also not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Avoid D_c. For the mismatch set S, use its area bound directly: ||tilde I||_{L2(S)}<=C h^{k/2}||tilde I||_{infinity}, and use the inverse trace bound ||v_h||_{L2(S)}<=C h^{-1/2}||v_h||_{L2(D_h)}. Together with the O(h^k) flux factor this gives O(h^{(3k-1)/2}), which suffices for k>=2.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed T3 argument does not yield its claimed exponent from the defined cell patch.
issues.title: The grazing-cell patch is assigned the volume of a much thinner boundary strip
issues.why_classification: Once the separate geometric measure issue is resolved, the paper's existing area and inverse estimates provide a routine local bypass preserving the claimed T3 rate.
